meta.headline: Organic farms do spray. Does eating organic still cut the pesticides you take in?
meta.seoTitle: Organic farming, pesticides and what reaches your body

dek.text: Organic rules allow listed pesticides once prevention fails, most of them milder on Europe's hazard tables though not all, and trials find pesticide levels in urine fall within days of eating organic.

assertions.text: Under the US organic regulations, when preventive practices are insufficient, a biological or botanical substance or a substance on the National List of allowed synthetics may be applied to prevent, suppress or control pests, weeds or diseases.
Most pesticides approved for EU organic agriculture are of comparatively low toxicological concern for consumers, with pyrethrins and copper as the notable exceptions.
qualifications: The qualification callout in question-1 says these are hazard classes for the EU list, not measured exposure, and names the exceptions.

assertions.text: All 4 whole-diet trials that measured urinary pesticide excretion found a significant difference between the conventional and organic phases, with reductions of up to 90% within a few days.

description.text: Organic farms may use listed pesticides, mostly but not all milder. Eating organic cuts residues and urinary pesticide levels, but not to nil.

sections.name: hook
sections.heading: Does organic mean nothing was sprayed?

sentences.text: Dr. Eric Berg tells his viewers that organic "means without pesticides herbicides fungicides and insecticides".

assertions.text: Dr. Eric Berg says organic means without pesticides, herbicides, fungicides and insecticides.

quote.text: means without pesticides herbicides fungicides and insecticides
quote.speaker: Dr. Eric Berg

sentences.text: If that were so, the organic rulebook would have nothing to say about spraying.
It has a good deal to say: the rules allow listed pesticides once prevention fails, and residue tests find organic food carries pesticides less often than conventional food, not never.

assertions.text: Under the US organic regulations, when preventive practices are insufficient, a biological or botanical substance or a substance on the National List of allowed synthetics may be applied to prevent, suppress or control pests, weeds or diseases.
Conventional produce was more likely to carry detectable residues than organic produce, but samples of organic produce frequently contained residues.
qualifications: The unresolved callout in question-2 gives what the residue comparisons cannot say.

sentences.text: This article takes the questions in turn: what organic farms may spray and how it compares, then what eating organic does to the pesticides in your body.

sections.name: question-1
sections.heading: Does organic farming really mean no pesticides, and are the ones it uses safer?

sentences.text: Dr. Mindy Pelz describes organic produce as "a food that has technically not been sprayed", and a College of Naturopathic Medicine video says organic growers rely on natural methods "instead of using chemicals".

assertions.text: Dr. Mindy Pelz describes organic food as a food that has technically not been sprayed.

quote.text: a food that has technically not been sprayed
quote.speaker: Dr. Mindy Pelz

assertions.text: The College of Naturopathic Medicine says organic agriculture relies on natural methods instead of using chemicals.

sentences.text: A speaker at a Harvard public health forum tells the audience the opposite, asking them to "banish that notion" that organic farming uses no pesticides.

assertions.text: A speaker at the Harvard forum says the notion that organic farming does not use pesticides should be banished.

sentences.text: The US regulations settle the first part: when a farm's preventive practices are not enough to control crop pests, weeds and diseases, it may apply a biological or botanical substance, or a synthetic one from the National List, provided the conditions of use are documented in its organic system plan.

assertions.text: Under the US organic regulations, when preventive practices are insufficient, a biological or botanical substance or a substance on the National List of allowed synthetics may be applied to prevent, suppress or control pests, weeds or diseases.

sentences.text: That list is titled "Synthetic substances allowed for use in organic crop production", and most of its entries may be used only once those preventive practices prove insufficient.

assertions.text: Section 205.601 lists synthetic substances allowed for use in organic crop production, most of which may only be used when preventive practices prove insufficient.

quote.text: Synthetic substances allowed for use in organic crop production

sentences.text: The US Department of Agriculture says most permitted pest-control materials are naturally derived, such as pyrethrum or Bacillus thuringiensis, and names elemental sulfur, insecticidal soap, horticultural oils and copper hydroxide among the synthetic ones allowed.

assertions.text: The USDA report says most pest control materials permitted in organic agriculture are naturally derived, such as pyrethrum and Bacillus thuringiensis.
The USDA report says synthetic pest control materials allowed in organic crop production include elemental sulfur, insecticidal soap, horticultural oils and copper hydroxide.

sentences.text: Europe's organic regulation lists paraffin oils, lime sulphur and several copper compounds, Bordeaux mixture among them, and limits copper hydroxide to uses totalling at most 28 kg of copper per hectare over 7 years.

assertions.text: The EU organic annex authorises paraffin oils, lime sulphur and copper compounds including Bordeaux mixture for organic production, copper hydroxide only in uses totalling at most 28 kg of copper per hectare over 7 years.

sentences.text: On whether those pesticides are gentler, Kurzgesagt says "Organic pesticides are not necessarily safer than conventional ones."

assertions.text: Kurzgesagt says organic pesticides are not necessarily safer than conventional ones.

quote.text: Organic pesticides are not necessarily safer than conventional ones.
quote.speaker: Kurzgesagt

sentences.text: Simnett Nutrition answers that "they're generally not as harmful and they're more closely regulated".

assertions.text: Simnett Nutrition says organic pesticides are generally not as harmful and more closely regulated.

quote.text: they're generally not as harmful and they're more closely regulated
quote.speaker: Simnett Nutrition

sentences.text: A review of organic food and health set the 385 substances authorised as pesticides in the EU beside the 26 of them also approved for organic farming, all evaluated under the same legal framework, and counted their hazard classes; the table below shows where the lists differ and where they overlap.

assertions.text: Of 385 substances authorised as pesticides in the EU, 26 are also approved for use in organic agriculture, evaluated in accordance with the same legal framework.

blocks.caption: Hazard classes among EU-approved pesticide substances: the full list against those approved for organic farming

cells.label: Active substances approved for organic farming

rows.label: With any identified toxicity (a set daily intake, acute reference dose or operator exposure level)
Candidates for substitution for a low acceptable intake or exposure level

cells.label: All EU-approved, low ADI, ARfD or AOEL
Organic-approved, low ADI, ARfD or AOEL

rows.label: Candidates for substitution for endocrine disrupting properties
Candidates for substitution for meeting two of the persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic criteria

cells.label: All EU-approved, two PBT criteria fulfilled

sentences.text: The contrast is sharpest where people worry most: 27 substances on the full list are classed as suspected human carcinogens, and none on the organic list is classed as a carcinogen or a reproductive toxicant.

assertions.text: 27 EU-approved pesticide substances are classed as carcinogenicity category 2, suspected human carcinogens, against 0 of those approved for organic farming, and 0 organic-approved substances are classed as reproductive toxicants.
qualifications: The qualification callout below says these are intrinsic hazard classes for the EU list, not exposure.

sentences.text: The review judges most organic-approved pesticides of comparatively low concern for consumers: some have no identified toxicity, some are ordinary nutrients or foods such as iron or rapeseed oil, and the synthetic pyrethroids lambda-cyhalothrin and deltamethrin are approved for insect traps only, with a negligible risk of entering the food chain.

assertions.text: Most pesticides approved for organic agriculture are of comparatively low toxicological concern for consumers because they have no identified toxicity, are part of a normal diet or nutrients, or are approved for insect traps only with a negligible risk of entering the food chain.
qualifications: The qualification callout below names the exceptions, pyrethrins and copper.

assertions.text: EU organic rules allow the synthetic pyrethroids lambda-cyhalothrin and deltamethrin, but only in certain insect traps.

sentences.text: These counts describe each substance's intrinsic hazard, irrespective of how it is used or how much of it anyone is exposed to, and they cover the pesticides approved in the EU.

assertions.text: The classifications relate to a compound's intrinsic hazardous properties, irrespective of its use and exposure pattern, and cover EU-approved substances.

sentences.text: The review also names the exceptions: pyrethrins, an extract of a chrysanthemum, "share the same mechanism of action as the synthetic pyrethroid insecticides", and copper, a nutrient, is toxic at high intakes and harmful to aquatic organisms.

assertions.text: Pyrethrins, a plant extract from Chrysanthemum cinerariaefolium approved for organic farming, share the same mechanism of action as the synthetic pyrethroid insecticides.

quote.text: share the same mechanism of action as the synthetic pyrethroid insecticides

assertions.text: Copper is an essential nutrient, although toxic at high intakes and of ecotoxicological concern due to toxicity to aquatic organisms.

sentences.text: So the organic list is milder on these tables, mostly but not wholly: it is not proof that every organic pesticide is safer than a synthetic alternative, and the tables measure hazard, not what reaches food.

assertions.text: Most pesticides approved for EU organic agriculture are of comparatively low toxicological concern for consumers, with pyrethrins and copper as the notable exceptions.
qualifications: The qualification callout in question-1 says these are hazard classes for the EU list, not measured exposure, and names the exceptions.

sentences.text: A crop meta-analysis states in its introduction that organic standards "prohibit the use of synthetic chemical crop protection products"; it is a passing background line in a study of crop composition, it does not examine the rules, and it cannot decide whether every synthetic pesticide is banned.

assertions.text: The Baranski meta-analysis introduction says organic crop production standards prohibit the use of synthetic chemical crop protection products.

quote.text: prohibit the use of synthetic chemical crop protection products

sentences.text: The sources split less than they seem to: the USDA says organic standards prohibit most synthetic substances, including most conventional pesticides, while the regulation itself lists the synthetic substances it allows, so "no synthetics" is a summary of the rule rather than the rule.

assertions.text: The USDA report says organic standards prohibit most synthetic substances, including most pesticides used in conventional agriculture, but lists synthetic pest control materials allowed in organic crop production.
Section 205.601 lists synthetic substances allowed for use in organic crop production.

sentences.text: That answers what organic farms may spray; the next question is what reaches the people who eat the food.

sections.name: question-2
sections.heading: Does eating organic actually lower the pesticides you take in?

sentences.text: A DW Documentary film puts it plainly: "the primary advantage of organic produce is that there are no pesticide residues".

assertions.text: DW Documentary says the primary advantage of organic produce is that there are no pesticide residues.

quote.text: the primary advantage of organic produce is that there are no pesticide residues
quote.speaker: DW Documentary

sentences.text: NutritionFacts.org says diet can "turn on and off urinary concentrations of pesticide metabolites like a light switch".

assertions.text: NutritionFacts.org says urinary concentrations of pesticide metabolites can be turned on and off like a light switch.

quote.text: turn on and off urinary concentrations of pesticide metabolites like a light switch
quote.speaker: NutritionFacts.org

sentences.text: Food monitoring finds organic food cleaner but not clean: averaged over the last three available years of EU testing, residues below the legal limits were found in 13.8% of organic samples against 43.7% of all samples, a comparison with every sample rather than with conventional food alone.

assertions.text: EFSA monitoring, averaged over the last 3 available years, reports pesticide residues below Maximum Residue Levels in 43.7% of all and 13.8% of organic food samples.
qualifications: The sentence says the comparison is against all samples, not conventional ones only.

sentences.text: In the US Pesticide Data Program, 23 percent of organic samples tested positive for pesticide residues.

assertions.text: PDP data indicated that 23 percent of organic food samples tested positive for pesticide residues.

blocks.caption: How often organic food carries pesticide residues, against all or conventional samples

rows.label: EU monitoring (EFSA), organic against all samples, residues below legal limits, last three available years

cells.label: Organic samples with residues below the MRL
All samples with residues below the MRL

rows.label: EU monitoring (EFSA), organic against all samples, over the legal limit
EU monitoring (EFSA), organic against all samples, over the acute reference dose
Meta-analysis of crop studies, organic against conventional crops, detectable residues

sentences.text: The amounts are lower too: an analysis of three US data sets found residue concentrations on organic samples consistently lower crop by crop, and state monitoring in Baden-Wuerttemberg in 2021 found an average of 0.002 mg/kg on organic fruit and vegetables against 0.48 mg/kg on conventional fruit and 0.40 mg/kg on conventional vegetables.

assertions.text: Baker et al., comparing specific residues on specific crops across 3 data sets, found residue concentrations in organic samples consistently lower than in conventional ones.
CVUA Stuttgart found average residues of 0.002 mg/kg in organic fruit and vegetable samples in 2021, against 0.48 mg/kg for conventional fruit and 0.40 mg/kg for conventional vegetables.

sentences.text: The meta-analysis figure counts how often crop samples carried detectable residues, not how much residue they carried; the amounts come from the US data sets and the German monitoring above.

assertions.text: The meta-analysis compared the frequency of occurrence of detectable pesticide residues in conventional and organic crops.

sentences.text: And fewer residues is not the same as a safer plate: the Stanford review found the risk of detectable residues 30 percentage points lower on organic produce, but only small differences in the risk of exceeding maximum allowed limits.

assertions.text: The risk of contamination with detectable pesticide residues was 30% lower among organic than conventional produce, but differences in risk for exceeding maximum allowed limits were small.

sentences.text: And those legal limits reflect a pesticide's approved use rather than the toxicological relevance of the residue, with no separate limits for organic products, so the residue counts say how often and how much, not how harmful.

assertions.text: Maximum Residue Levels reflect the approved use of a pesticide rather than the toxicological relevance of the residue, and there are no separate MRLs for organic products.

sentences.text: What reaches the body has been measured directly: a systematic review found four whole-diet trials, two in children and two in adults, that tested pesticides in urine, and all of them found a significant difference between the conventional and organic phases.

assertions.text: 4 whole-diet crossover trials, 2 in children and 2 in adults, measured urinary pesticide excretion, and all of them found a significant difference in pesticide metabolites excreted between the diet phases.

sentences.text: The reduction was in most cases dramatic, up to 90 percent, and came within a few days.

assertions.text: The reduction was in most cases dramatic, up to 90% during the organic phase, and occurred within a few days.

sentences.text: A small study of 16 people in four US families, comparing days on non-organic food with days on organic food, found urinary levels of 13 pesticide compounds fell significantly, and an analysis of the same families' 158 urine samples found mean glyphosate fell 70.93 percent within six days on the organic diet.

assertions.text: In 16 participants from 4 US families, 158 urine samples, an organic diet was followed by significant reductions in urinary levels of 13 pesticide metabolites and parent compounds.
In the same 4 US families, 16 participants and 158 urine samples, mean urinary glyphosate decreased 70.93% within 6 days on an organic diet.

rows.label: Whole-diet trials in children and adults, systematic review

cells.label: Reduction in urinary pesticide metabolites, up to

sentences.text: So eating organic does lower the pesticides you take in, sharply and within days, though organic food still often carries some residue.

assertions.text: Switching to an organic diet significantly lowers urinary pesticide metabolites within a few days.
Conventional produce was more likely to carry detectable residues than organic produce, but samples of organic produce frequently contained residues.
qualifications: The unresolved callout in question-2 gives what the residue comparisons cannot say.

sentences.text: Whether that lower exposure makes anyone healthier is a separate question these trials do not answer; a review of farming systems notes that lower residues may not translate into better health outcomes.

assertions.text: Clark and Tilman note that organic foods carry lower pesticide residues, although the difference may not translate into improved human health outcomes.

sections.name: close
sections.heading: What the organic label does and does not promise

sentences.text: Put together, the answers separate the field from the plate.
The label tells you which sprays a farm was allowed and when, not that nothing was sprayed, and what it buys you is less pesticide in your food and your body rather than none.

assertions.text: Under the US organic regulations, when preventive practices are insufficient, a biological or botanical substance or a substance on the National List of allowed synthetics may be applied to prevent, suppress or control pests, weeds or diseases.
Conventional produce was more likely to carry detectable residues than organic produce, but samples of organic produce frequently contained residues.
qualifications: The unresolved callout in question-2 gives what the residue comparisons cannot say.

sentences.text: When a video promises pesticide-free food, ask which pesticides, used when, and how much of them reaches your plate.
